_readme: docs/PLAN/07 § Demo Data: this is a seeded invitation owned by a system account, in
the same tables as any other invitation, so the catalogue demo renders through the
production renderer reading the production public API shape. There is no second code
It must fill EVERY required_field of the reference template, and a test asserts
exactly that with P0-20's collectMissingRequiredFields -- so a demo that stopped
being renderable would fail before anyone saw a half-empty catalogue page.
The content is Indonesian because the product is (docs/PLAN/00). A demo in English
would set the wrong expectation on the one page whose job is setting expectations.

_gallery_note: Six media rows, one cover. The BYTES are not seeded -- see seed.mts. The rows exist
so the demo satisfies the gallery section's required_fields and so the renderer has
the shape it expects; the images themselves arrive with the upload pipeline (P1-16)
or as template assets. Stated here rather than discovered by whoever opens the demo
page and sees six broken images.
_settings_note: enabled_sections omits `gift`, matching the reference template's
enabled_by_default: false for that section. The demo therefore also demonstrates a
disabled configurable section, which is the case BR-4.1 is about: the gift accounts
above are stored and simply not displayed.
hero and event are absent from this list ON PURPOSE. They are configurable: false,
so docs/FRONTEND/04 step 2 renders them regardless -- and if this list were the only
thing keeping them on screen, a test asserting that would be asserting nothing.
_guestbook_note: A few approved entries so the guestbook section has something to render. Moderation
is on, and one entry is left pending on purpose: the demo should show what an
unmoderated message looks like to nobody, which is the correct answer.
